summary: Lewis County, NY tower built by the Conservation Department in 1950, closed 1970 and dismantled 1982; now standing at Thompson Park Zoo in Watertown.

facts.agency: New York Conservation Department (built); Thompson Park Zoo, Watertown (current host)
facts.status_note: Structure moved to Thompson Park Zoo in Watertown; no source read describes the New Boston site today

access.note: On display on the Thompson Park Zoo grounds in Watertown. Sources disagree on when it reopened (2004 or 2016). Climbing today is not confirmed.

events.note: Erected by the Conservation Department as an 80-foot Aermotor LS40 at New Boston
Closed at the end of the 1970 season with the advent of aerial detection
Dismantled by DEC personnel and moved to facilities in Harrisville
Moved into Thompson Park Zoo, Watertown, as a community educational exhibit (2016 report)
Zoo restored the tower on its grounds; it stayed closed to the public until liability insurance was secured
Grand opening at the zoo that summer; the 2004 report says the tower is open to the public
FFLA $500 grant for repairs; work completed in the spring. The chapter's list says it reopened to the public at the zoo in 2016

notes_for_editor: Structure history rests on the chapter's own pages and reports. Sources disagree on when the tower was first reopened: the 2004 annual report says it was open after a summer 2004 grand opening, while the chapter list says it reopened in 2016. Current climbing access is unconfirmed. The relocated record us-ny-new-boston-at-thompson-park-zoo already holds Watertown history; this story covers the original site and the move. A web search snippet mentioned climbing at the Thompson Park tower, but that page was not read and is not cited. The DEC fire towers page was checked and does not mention New Boston, so it is not cited.
